subject: Re: GreenSky Logistics — request for virtual-card onboarding / PO exception
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@greenskylogistics.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: virtual-card onboarding + PO exemption for pilot

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the team at GreenSky Logistics is excited to move a small pilot forward. One operational ask before we can start: our AP process prefers virtual card settlement instead of a standing purchase order. For this 90‑day pilot we'll be transacting via virtual cards at invoice time.

Can Redwood accept virtual‑card payments without a formal PO on file for pilots under $25k? If not, can we get an exception for this pilot?

I attached our vendor intake (PDF) and insurance cert — happy to fill any forms you need.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Procurement
GreenSky Logistics
attachments: greensky_onboard_intake.pdf (application/pdf), insurance_cert_2028.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@greenskylogistics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Nov 2028 10:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: virtual-card onboarding + PO exemption for pilot

Hi Elena — great to hear, and glad the demo landed.

Short answer: we can make an exception for a short pilot, but we need Procurement to sign off on limits + evidence checks (insurance, W‑9, bank details) and for Legal to confirm commercial terms for card settlement. I’ve attached our standard vendor onboarding form — please complete the highlighted fields (tax id, remit address, ACH fallback) and return.

Next steps I propose:
- Elena: return the completed onboarding form + W‑9 (we have your insurance attachment already)
- Procurement (David): review and approve a no‑PO virtual‑card workflow for pilot up to $25k; specify any additional controls (monthly cap, single‑transaction limits)
- Marissa (RevOps): confirm billing code / subscription flow so cost centre tagging is correct

I’ll keep this thread in case we need to escalate.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Manager, Partner Success
Redwood Inference
attachments: vendor_onboarding_form.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Nov 2028 11:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: GreenSky Logistics — virtual card exception (internal)

David — quick tag. Naomi looped procurement; GreenSky asks to be onboarded using virtual cards for a pilot under $25k with no standing PO. They provided insurance and intake.

Can procurement approve a temporary waiver and if so what controls should we attach (billing contact, monthly cap, required invoice metadata)? They will need a HubSpot link and a DocuSign for the vendor agreement.

Short replies welcome — we need to get Elena an answer today so pilot onboarding isn't delayed.

—Marissa
Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Nov 2028 13:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: GreenSky Logistics — virtual card exception (internal)

Naomi / Marissa — I’m okay with a temporary PO exception for this pilot with the following conditions:
1) Pilot not to exceed $25,000 total and no single transaction > $7,500.
2) GreenSky must complete our onboarding form + W‑9; proofs of insurance are required (we have the cert but confirm effective dates).
3) Card settlement allowed only after Redwood issues an invoice that includes: Redwood invoice number, HubSpot company ID (67890), and cost center tag.
4) RevOps (Marissa) to set monthly cap alerts and prevent auto‑renewal without PO compliance.
5) Exception expires 90 days from onboarding date; procurement to be notified 7 days before expiry for either extension or enforcement of PO requirement.

If Elena can accept those controls, I approve the exception. Please document in HubSpot and attach the signed onboarding form and the DocuSign link to the procurement record.

David Kim
Director, Procurement
Redwood Inference
attachments: procurement_exception_template.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@greenskylogistics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Nov 2028 10:25:00 -08:00
Subject: GreenSky Logistics — exception approved (virtual card pilot)

Hi Elena — good news: Procurement approved a time‑limited exception for virtual‑card settlement for your 90‑day pilot with the controls below. If you agree, we’ll route the vendor agreement and onboarding via DocuSign this afternoon.

Approved controls (summary):
- Pilot cap: $25,000 total; single tx limit $7,500
- Required docs: completed onboarding form (attached), W‑9, current insurance certificate
- Invoice metadata: include Redwood invoice number, HubSpot company ID 67890, and cost center tag on each invoice
- RevOps: monthly cap alert active; no auto‑renewal without PO compliance
- Exception expires 90 days from onboarding; procurement will notify 7 days before expiry

Next steps for GreenSky:
1) Please complete the attached vendor_onboarding_form.pdf and return with a W‑9.
2) Confirm you accept the caps/conditions in writing.
3) I’ll send a DocuSign for the vendor agreement once we have the returned form.

Link to HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890
DocuSign (will be sent): https://redwood.inference/ds/onboard/green-sky-docusign

Thanks — if you confirm today we can kick off billing and issue the first virtual card once onboarding is complete.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Manager, Partner Success
Redwood Inference
